chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: She starts to write arrangements
summary: She gave ideas at rehearsals that Andy took down, then wrote her first full arrangement for him. She describes finding unusual chords that he said broke the rules.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Once the band got to Kansas City, was that when you started to write.
Yes, write. Andy knew that I had ideas - I was writing all along but I couldn't write it down. I'd give them

ideas during the rehearsal. Maybe they wanted to play a song like "Singing in the Rain" and I'd say, "Well, listen to this." Andy would take it down real fast but sometimes they didn't at all. In Kansas City he'd come to the house like 10 o'clock in the morning and sit there till 12. I said, I can't go through this, so after about 2 weeks or a week or so he came down and I had an arrangement ready for him. The only thing that wasn't really balanced right was the tenor and the trombones and he showed me that. From that day on I began writing.
Were you just doing this from instinct then, the writing?
I watched him. I can learn a lot through watching. That was my bag, see, watching people and doing what they do.
All this period, this two years when you're traveling with the band and just occasionally getting to play, how did you feel? Did you feel that you were going anywhere?

No, it wasn't that; I thought I was helping. There's a peculiar thing about me in life. You know if you want to really hear me play or write something, give me somebody to help. If I think that I'm helping a situation, somebody say, Mary come out to the church and do something and help us and do this - it's amazing the work that I can

do and I'm very happy with my work. That's been my bag since I've been born. If I think I'm helping someone I get great things going and I was helping them in a way. I discovered chords and Andy used to say to me, "You can't do that. It's against the rules of writing music." I said, "But I hear a sixth in this chord." He said, "But you can't do it." I said, "I'm going to do it." I did the arrangement of, before I did "Walkin'", trumpet and 3 saxophones. We only had 3 saxophones and one trumpet and trombone, something like that. So what I did, I put a trumpet in and I had 3 saxophones to play 4-part harmony. He kept telling me it was against the rules of the chord. In that year I guess it was but I was hearing - I found these things on the piano and I said, this will sound good - it sounds good here. After a while I started arranging it.
